card: This PR implements the validation logic for BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) with activation configured exclusively on regtest via BIP 9. It addresses long-standing consensus flaws including quadratic legacy sigops processing DoS, 64-byte transaction Merkle tree collisions, timewarp attacks, negative difficulty adjustment periods, and coinbase height timelocks. Over 95% of the diff consists of test vectors, unit tests, and functional test suites adapted from Bitcoin Inquisition. It establishes the consensus verification rules in Core ahead of any future deployment decisions on production networks.
changed_since_previous: Rebased onto master following the merge of PR #35949 (miner Murch-Zawy rule enforcement) with minor test and code adjustments.

enables: BIP 54 testing and future mainnet deployment consideration

evidence: Author notes the patchset is ported from logic 'reviewed and tested on Bitcoin Inquisition' with companion miner PR #35949 already merged into master

Commit messages and comments cite prevention of 'flaws in the Merkle tree algorithm that make it so that such transactions may be re-interpreted as inner tree nodes (CVE-2017-12842)' and timewarp / Murch-Zawy exploits
problem: Bitcoin consensus retains legacy vulnerabilities, including quadratic legacy sigop CPU exhaustion, potential Merkle tree internal node collision exploits (CVE-2017-12842) via 64-byte transactions, timewarp attacks against difficulty calculation, and duplicate coinbase transaction risks. Developers and node operators currently cannot exercise or test the BIP 54 validation engine in Bitcoin Core in preparation for any future soft fork activation.

risk.why: Any flaw in consensus validation logic or block verification constraints can cause chain splits, consensus disagreements, or node crashes.

scope_notes: More than 5,700 lines of the diff are JSON test vectors and unit tests (notably `bip54_timestamps.json` and `bip54_tests.cpp`). Several existing functional tests required configuration overrides (`-vbparams=consensuscleanup:0:0`) or updated coinbase templates because the rules are enabled by default on regtest.
summary: Implements the BIP 54 (Consensus Cleanup) soft fork validation rules, enabled exclusively on regtest using BIP 9 versionbits deployment bit 3 while remaining inactive on mainnet, testnet, and signet. The consensus rules cap legacy (non-Segwit) sigops per transaction at 2,500, invalidate 64-byte transactions to prevent Merkle tree collisions, constrain difficulty adjustment period timestamps to block timewarp and negative retarget intervals, and require coinbase transactions to be timelocked to block height minus one. Over 95% of the patch consists of unit tests, JSON test vectors, fuzzing harnesses, and functional test coverage.
